tasks.notes: Kill-pattern hole the sibling write path already closes: a pattern carrying a shell expansion is not statically resolvable, but `bashKillPatterns` hands it to `killPatternMatches` as a literal. `pkill -f "$FLEET_TEST_CMD"` (or `pkill -f $(cat cmd)`) yields the pattern text `$FLEET_TEST_CMD`, which matches neither `claude` nor the TEST COMMAND value, so the hook allows the exact kill the fix exists to refuse — while ten lines below, `decide()` denies a *write* target on `/[$`]/` for precisely this reason (fleet/confine-hook.mjs:237-240, "Deny rather than resolve a value we cannot know"). No Machine clause names this form and no exam leg exercises it, so it is advisory, not blocking; the residual the task's Context concedes is a pattern matching *another prompt line*, not an unresolvable one. Denying a kill pattern containing `$` or a backtick costs nothing at BASE (no BASE test names `pkill`/`killall`, confirmed by grep over the tree) and keeps the two halves of the same function consistent.; plan-defect: M5's "first `TEST COMMAND:` line wins" (pinned by exam leg (v)) is right for the impl and exam dispatches and wrong for the fix dispatches. The engine builds `examinerInputs`/`implementerInputs` as `testCmdLine(...) + sharedInputs` (fleet/run-engine.mjs:1009-1010), so its line precedes the task body there — but the two fix dispatches build `roles.fix + taskBodyBlock(task, wavesPath) + testCmdLine(task, workerTestCmd) + …` (fleet/run-engine.mjs:1358 and :1575), body FIRST. On a fix round for a task whose body happens to carry a line beginning `TEST COMMAND:` (a Proof `Run:` block, a plan quoting an exam command), `childEnvFor` would take that quoted line and the hook would compare kill patterns against a command the worker was never handed. The implementer transcribed the clause faithfully and cannot diverge from it — leg (v) grades exactly this — so the change belongs outside this task's FILES: either reorder fleet/run-engine.mjs:1358/:1575 to put `testCmdLine` before `taskBodyBlock`, or amend M5 to name the LAST occurrence. Bounded impact (a heuristic guard reads a slightly wrong string), hence minor. The justification comment at fleet/run-worker.mjs:751-756 of the patch ("the engine writes one … and a later occurrence is task body quoting it") overstates this for the fix prompts and is worth a hedge either way.; unverified: the seam between the two halves of the claim is asserted nowhere. test_run_worker.mjs legs (u)-(w) pin that the child spawn's env carries `FLEET_TEST_CMD`, and test_confine_hook.mjs legs (a)-(t) pin that the hook reads `process.env.FLEET_TEST_CMD` — but nothing exercises the step in between, that Claude Code propagates the worker's env to the PreToolUse hook process it spawns. If it did not, every M1 leg would still pass and the guard would be inert on every live dispatch. This is the split the task's own Proof specifies, so it is advisory, not a defect in the diff; a leg in fleet/tests/probe_confine_live.mjs (which already builds a `createRunWorker` with `promptFileFor`/`settingsFor` at :66) dispatching a prompt with a `TEST COMMAND:` line and a hostile `pkill -f <that command>` and reading the resulting `confine-denials.jsonl` line would settle it end to end.; plan-defect: `first TEST COMMAND: line wins` is only correct for the impl/exam dispatch. `childEnvFor` (fleet/run-worker.mjs) takes the first `/^TEST COMMAND:[ \t]*(.+)$/m` match, and its comment justifies this as "the engine writes one (`testCmdLine`, run-engine.mjs), and a later occurrence is task body quoting it". That holds at fleet/run-engine.mjs:1009-1010, where `testCmdLine(...)` is prepended to `sharedInputs` (which ends in `taskBodyBlock`). It does NOT hold for the two fix-round prompts, fleet/run-engine.mjs:1358 and fleet/run-engine.mjs:1575, both composed as `roles.fix + taskBodyBlock(task, wavesPath) + testCmdLine(task, workerTestCmd) + ...` — the task body comes FIRST there. `taskBodyBlock` inlines `task.body` verbatim (`'\nTASK:\n' + task.body`, run-engine.mjs:417), so any plan body carrying a column-0 `TEST COMMAND:` line makes every `fix:<id>` dispatch export that body's value as FLEET_TEST_CMD instead of the command the fix worker was actually handed. Impact is bounded — the body-quoted string is still text in the `claude -p` argv, so denying on it is still a true self-match, and the real command merely falls back into the residual the task already concedes ("a pattern that matches some other line of the prompt ... is not caught") — but the fix round is precisely the lane where an implementer reaches for `pkill -f <the stuck test>`. This is not answerable inside this task: M5 and Proof leg (v) pin first-wins, and the exam (leg (v)) grades it, so changing `childEnvFor` here would fail the submission's own grading. The fix lies in `fleet/run-engine.mjs` — a sibling-owned path outside this task's FILES — by moving `testCmdLine(task, workerTestCmd)` ahead of `taskBodyBlock(task, wavesPath)` in those two prompt expressions, which also makes the fix round match the ordering the impl/exam dispatch already uses.; unverified: a kill pattern carrying a shell expansion is not statically resolvable and is silently allowed, where the same hook explicitly denies the analogous write target. `decide()` at fleet/confine-hook.mjs:237 (BASE) refuses a write whose target matches `/[$`]/` with "contains a shell expansion that cannot be resolved statically"; the new kill branch has no counterpart, so `pkill -f "$CMD"` yields the literal pattern `$CMD`, matches neither `claude` nor FLEET_TEST_CMD, and allows — while the shell kills whatever `$CMD` expands to. I am not proposing a deny here: M3 legs (o)/(r) require that a worker can still stop a server it started, and a blanket expansion deny on kill patterns would false-deny exactly those. What is worth fixing is the disclosure — the new residual comment at fleet/confine-hook.mjs ("the conceded residual is the rest of the argv — a pattern matching a FILES path or a word of the task body") names only the argv-coverage gap, so a later reader who sees the expansion deny two screens below will reasonably assume this branch closes the same class. Add the expansion case to that residual sentence. What would settle it either way is a leg pinning the chosen behaviour for `pkill -f "$CMD"`; none exists, and no Machine clause names the form.

fleet/run-engine.mjs — in the examiner-alone re-dispatch, the catch that swallows a second failure binds `e2` and never uses it: the only record of why the second attempt failed is `log('task <id> examiner died again — proceeding unexamined')`, which carries no message, and the report's judgmentCalls then say only the generic `examiner returned no reply — no exam recorded; the implementer proceeds unexamined` from the verdict block. The first death's message IS recorded (`task <id>: examiner died (<msg>)`), so an operator reading a run where both attempts died sees the first cause and nothing at all for the second — including the case where it was `cutExamClone`/`bootstrapExamClone` that threw rather than the agent, which is a different failure entirely. M2 asserts only the generic wording, so this blocks nothing, but appending `e2`'s message to the log line (or to a judgment call) costs one string concat and keeps the second death diagnosable.; Second-death message is dropped from the run record. In the new re-dispatch block in `fleet/run-engine.mjs`, `catch (e2) { ex = null; log(...) }` binds `e2` and never uses it: the only durable trace of why the second examiner died is the `log()` line (a noop in the sims and not part of `report`). The judgment call the operator actually reads then comes from the pre-existing verdict block — `task T1: examiner returned no reply — no exam recorded; the implementer proceeds unexamined` — which does not say a second dispatch was made or why it failed. M2 asks only for that wording, so nothing is unverified, but the first death's message is recorded (`examiner died (<msg>)`) while the second's is not, which is an asymmetry in the driver's own record. Suggested fix: in the catch, `judgmentCalls.push('task ' + task.id + ': the re-dispatched examiner died too (' + String((e2 && e2.message) || e2) + ') — proceeding unexamined')` before setting `ex = null`; leg (b)'s filter (`startsWith('task T1: examiner') && includes('proceeds unexamined')`) would still match exactly one entry as long as the new line's wording avoids `proceeds unexamined` (use `proceeding unexamined`, as above).

completenessFindings.detail: Task 1, Claim/Context (`fleet/confine-hook.mjs:222-247`, `bashKillPatterns`): an unquoted `killall` token is treated as a kill wherever it sits, and `full` is set unconditionally for it, so a *search* for the word — e.g. `git grep killall fleet/` or `grep -rn killall fleet/tests/` — is read as a kill whose pattern is the following path token and is tried against `FLEET_TEST_CMD`. With the live value (`node fleet/tests/test_confine_hook.mjs`), `new RegExp('fleet/').test(testCmd)` is true, so the command is denied with a reason that tells the worker to `kill <pid>` instead. The same shape lets an option's *value* become a pattern (`pkill --signal TERM -f claude` collects `TERM` as a pattern alongside `claude`). This is inside the contract — the Claim scopes the check to a command 'whose argv contains `pkill -f`/`killall`' and the Context specifies the kill be found 'WHEREVER it sits' — and it errs fail-closed, so it does not stop the merge; but it is reachable by a worker grepping this very code, and the deny reason misdescribes what it refused. Worth an issue: require the kill token to be in command position (index 0, or after a `|`/`;`/`&&`/`cd` boundary) rather than anywhere in the token stream.
